themes.label: Unauthorized charges and refund failures
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android report being charged unexpectedly, including double charges on rides and Uber Eats orders, post-cancellation fees, lingering Uber One subscription billing after cancelling, and reversed promotional discounts. Many say refunds were promised by support agents but never arrived, and they feel support is automated, circular, or unreachable, often via AI chat.
themes.recommendation: Audit billing logs for cancelled Uber One subscriptions, duplicate authorization captures, and promotion reversals on Rides and Eats, and add a refund-status tracker with a guaranteed human escalation path for disputed charges.

themes.label: Final fare higher than booked
themes.summary: Riders on Android report that the fare shown at booking is later replaced by a much higher amount at drop-off, often because the driver's app displays a different total or the route is changed. Many feel support only offers auto-replies or Uber Cash credit rather than resolving the mismatch, and some describe the lower quoted price as a bait.
themes.recommendation: Investigate fare-lock logic on Android by reproducing a booking that is opened, backgrounded, and reopened, then compare the rider app, driver app, and receipt totals to find where the quoted price is recalculated and whether route or congestion adjustments are applied without consent.

themes.label: Drivers cancel accepted rides
themes.summary: Riders across Android and iOS describe long waits for a driver to accept, then drivers cancelling after acceptance, sometimes after the rider has already waited 20 to 60 minutes. Many say the app's ETA or timer is misleading, that they are charged cancellation fees even when the driver caused the delay, and that re-matching then starts the wait over. Several also report surge or extra fees being pushed when a scheduled or priority ride goes unmatched.
themes.recommendation: Pull driver cancellation and post-accept no-show data for the last 90 days, segmented by app version (v4.638 to v4.648) and by ride type, and investigate whether the matching or re-matching logic is causing the surge in cancellations. Pair that with a fix that waives rider cancellation fees when the driver cancels or fails to arrive within the ETA.

themes.label: Ride acceptance and cancellations
themes.summary: Riders describe long waits to get a driver to accept or show up, with requests searching for extended periods, drivers cancelling after accepting, and pickups delayed 30 to 45 minutes or more. Many feel the problem is worst during urgent situations, rush hours, bad weather, and early mornings, and some link it to surge pricing and a perceived shortage of drivers.
themes.recommendation: Pull matching and cancellation logs for the last 90 days, segmented by time of day, weather, and market, to measure driver acceptance rate, post-accept cancellation rate, and time to match, then prioritise a fix for post-accept driver cancellations and show realistic pickup ETAs at booking.

themes.label: Unreachable support and unresolved refunds
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say customer support is effectively unreachable, with the Help flow routing them through an automated AI bot that loops them back to the same options or auto-closes tickets. Many describe refunds for wrong, late, cancelled or charged-but-undelivered orders being denied, offered as small credits, or left pending for weeks, with some reporting accounts disabled or charged membership fees they cannot cancel.
themes.recommendation: Audit the Help and support escalation flow end to end, starting with a sample of tickets auto-closed by the bot in the last 90 days, and add a guaranteed path to a human agent for any refund or charge dispute above a set threshold.

themes.label: Overcharges, unreliable pickups, poor support
themes.summary: Users in this cluster report being charged more than expected, including doubled fares, duplicate charges, and fees they did not understand, alongside late or cancelled driver pickups even after paying extra. Many say they cannot reach human support when a payment, lost item, or wrong pickup goes wrong, and several mention uninstalling. The mix spans Android and iOS and recent versions, with a few reviews also citing a newer layout and location-entry problems.
themes.recommendation: Audit the fare and charge pipeline for duplicate or doubled transactions on Apple Pay and card payments, and add an in-app dispute flow that is reachable from the trip history screen and routes to a human agent within a defined SLA.

themes.label: Praise: friendly, professional drivers
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are praising individual drivers for being friendly, polite, punctual, and safe, with several noting clean cars and pleasant conversation. The feedback is uniformly positive and centers on the driver's personal service rather than the app itself. No complaints or feature requests appear in these reviews.
themes.recommendation: Identify the driver-rating and compliments signals behind these reviews and surface positive driver feedback to drivers (or use it in driver recognition programs) so the team can protect the behaviors riders are rewarding, such as punctuality, cleanliness, and courteous conversation.

themes.label: Praise: driver service quality
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are praising their drivers as professional, punctual, courteous, and helpful, with some mentioning help with luggage and groceries and accommodation for seniors and people with disabilities. Reviews are mostly short and written in English and French, and the cluster contains no complaints or feature requests.
themes.recommendation: Identify the driver behaviours that earn these comments (punctuality, luggage assistance, accessibility accommodation) and surface them as recognised driver badges or rider-facing highlights, while keeping them in the driver quality metrics used for rating and incentives.

reviews.t: The most recent update is frustrating
reviews.x: I’ve noticed several changes in recent updates that have significantly worsened my experience using the Uber app. Previously, the app automatically detected my current location when I opened it, which made requesting rides fast and convenient. Now, I have to manually enter my pickup location every time, which adds unnecessary friction and has pushed me to start using Lyft instead. Additionally, managing a business account has become very difficult. The app only allows me to enter credit card information from my current country (Canada), which does not work for my business setup. I also attempted to contact support through the app but never received a response. On top of that, the support chat text field is extremely buggy. It often fails to register what I type, forcing me to repeatedly tap and re-enter messages. Support then asked me to upload an image to explain my issue, but unfortunately, the image upload feature is also not working on mobile. Overall, these issues have made the app frustrating and unreliable to use. I hope the team can review these problems and improve the user experience soon.

I had taken a ride with one of the drivers and as I exited the car I noticed that my glasses were still in there. After contacting the driver he confirmed that the glasses were indeed in his car, within the span of 15 minutes. I had asked the driver if he would be able to return the glasses, even offered to pay addition (fuel expenses, etc). He insisted that I follow up with Uber to have them email him and charge me $15 to have him bring them back. Fast forward 2 months. I had continued communication through Uber’s Help assistance and finally was able to connect with the driver who had passed the glasses along to his “friend” who agreed to deliver it to me since the driver lived 30/40minutes away. Initially, I thought this would work out for all parties since the driver lived so far and if his friend was willing. My main concerns were disclosing my home address to the driver’s “friend” who had nothing to do with Uber and after two months, I wanted to see if the glasses were even mine to begin with. All the while, going back and forth between the driver/his friend/and Uber, being told that he refused to deliver the glasses if I didn’t pay $40. Upon arrival the driver’s friend refused to let me examine my glasses to see if it was indeed mine. He insisted that I e-transferred him $40 in addition to the $15 lost item return charge. In the end I had to call local authorities because this man was sitting in front of my house refusing to return my prescription glasses which I need for work and studying. It’s very unfortunate that this was not handled better by Uber support and by the driver. As I said in the beginning, I had no problem paying the driver to return the glasses ($15+ additional for time/expenses) but the fact that I had to call the local authorities just to have the driver’s friend show me the glasses (and struggling for the two months without my prescribed glasses to help me see). In the end, I’m happy to have my glasses returned because it would have taken longer to order new ones given covid. I do wish that Uber look into their support procedures to ensure that items aren’t being moved through outside of Uber driver contractors.

reviews.t: iOS11 let’s you do this anyway. Poor marketing attempt
reviews.x: iOS 11 gives users the right to set location services to “only while app is in use” to combat the slimy behaviour Uber popularized with the - either you always let us see your location or you don’t use our app crap that they tried to push down on consumers. The update in iOS 11 is a direct response to this slimy behaviour. Don’t try and market it as anything else.
